plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, the 3-era timeline completes: 17 Feb 1842 & 1844 (William Bowman maps Bowman's capsule at King's College London; Carl Ludwig proposes hydrostatic glomerular ultrafiltration) · 1 Oct 1924 & 1934 (Joseph Wearn & Alfred Newton Richards puncture a living frog glomerulus with a quartz micropipette to prove filtration and reabsorption; Homer Smith & James Shannon use inulin to measure human GFR at 125 mL/min = 180 L/day) · 17 Mar 1943 – 11 Sep 1945 (Willem Kolff builds the rotating-drum cellophane sausage-casing artificial kidney in Nazi-occupied Kampen and saves Patient #16 Sofia Schafstadt).

teach_overlay.detail: Animated timeline (1842 → 1960) alongside an inked comparison of Bowman's nephron and Kolff's rotating-drum / modern hollow-fibre dialyser
teach_overlay.scale: from a 25-year-old surgeon's microscope in London to a hair-thin quartz needle in Philadelphia and forty metres of sausage skin in wartime Holland, scientists unlocked the two-million-filter cleaning plant that keeps our blood pure
